shellParser.strategy: Owned parser starting from the pinned Bashkit revision, with freely maintained local changes and upstream parser tests retained unless a deliberate behavior change is recorded.

changeLog.classification: Original literal function-name retention adapter over the owned Bashkit parser at 491c3281f668b76d64b15210b8f5d7bf97244be0, crates/bashkit/src/parser/{mod.rs,ast.rs,print_cmd.rs}; no new upstream implementation copied.
changeLog.change: The two existing function parsers retain current_raw token spelling instead of normalized Word text. Document the existing FunctionDef.name contract. Preserve partial quotes, escapes, literal backticks, alias-produced names and raw line continuations in admitted AST copies. The function printer removes real continuations through the existing raw normalizer while retaining escaped backslashes and single-quoted text; backtick contents follow Bash continuation rules. Raw-normalizer traversal charges accept the existing optional quota, preserving bounded admission and unbounded function_string and command-substitution Word Display callers. Original regressions cover bounded/unbounded continuation, ANSI-C and localized-name parity without extending accepted grammar. No token recognition, grammar or public type changes.
changeLog.reason: Execution must reject expansion/quoted names with status 1 only when a declaration runs, while ordinary punctuation and literal backticks remain names. Existing raw provenance avoids an extra execution-time lexer and its allocations. The original interpreter adapter validates cooperatively and normalizes only real line continuations in the owned name buffer, respecting escaped backslashes within literal backticks. Escaped POSIX and fully quoted function grammar remain an Approved prerequisite, not a weakened comparison.

changeLog.classification: Original public bounded function-layout adapter over the existing owned Bash-layout printer; no additional upstream implementation copied. GNU Bash 5.3.15 supplies command -V observations.
changeLog.change: Expose function_string_bounded using the same PrintQuota, cooperative traversal, reconstruction admission and deferred-heredoc handling as bounded command labels. Share the pre-existing function layout between bounded and unbounded entries. Add allocation-before-copy, work/cancellation/timeout and layout-parity controls without changing upstream assertions.
changeLog.reason: Function-aware command -V reporting needs Bash function formatting without an unbounded function_string allocation. Reuse the existing printer instead of reparsing or copying retained function ASTs.

changeLog.change: Original structured conditional adapter over the existing locally maintained Bashkit parser: replace the token-word Conditional payload with boxed TestExpr nodes; preserve operator identity, quote spelling, grouping, grammar-positioned newline acceptance and flat logical chains at parse time; admit existing process-substitution word tokens in for-list grammar; print and statically validate the structured tree; admit its clone storage cooperatively. Add original bounded [[ ]] evaluation with lazy logical branches, scalar operands, quote-aware basic patterns, arithmetic comparisons and shared unary/file metadata test predicates. Charge conditional scalar captures, transient numeric formatting and recursive admitted expansion futures before allocation. Add an opt-in for-list fields adapter with admitted snapshots, segments, output buffers and futures through brace reparsing; preserve ordinary argv and diagnostic accounting. Extend the existing original pattern-positionals adapter with a conditional scalar mode, preserving case's first-field behavior.
changeLog.reason: The engine must execute [[ ]] without reinterpreting expanded operator-looking text, expanding skipped branches, or guessing unsupported predicates. All added runtime traversal, recursion and allocation use the command work/storage budget and cancellation checkpoints. No upstream implementation or upstream test assertion was copied or weakened; new parser and engine regressions are original. The separate original bounded no-capture ERE adapter is classified under shellControlFlow; unsupported regex constructs fail explicitly rather than using an unmetered fallback.

changeLog.change: Extend the original limits adapter with a synchronous cancellation probe at parser work-budget checkpoints. No copied parser implementation or upstream assertions changed.
changeLog.reason: Browser SIGINT must be observed while WASM is CPU-running, without waiting for the JavaScript worker event loop. The shell checks runtime_proc.interrupted through its foreground cancellation probe.

changeLog.change: Original parser-only error, limits and WASI clock adapters around the initial Bashkit parser import.
changeLog.reason: Expose a standalone parser crate with explicit input, work and cancellation limits.

changeLog.change: Replace the source byte-identity requirement with this base-revision and change record. No upstream parser behavior or tests changed.
changeLog.reason: The parser is maintained as our own code; fixes may diverge freely from Bashkit.

changeLog.change: Keep double-quoted parameter operand backslashes raw, preserve nested ${...} inside literal apostrophe spans, and treat raw escapes and existing lexer protection as indivisible when matching operand and quoted-word boundaries. Share the double-quote and literal-apostrophe span scanner. No upstream tests removed or changed. An explicit quote-context stack resumes outer spans after nested parameters and includes enclosing depth in the substitution ceiling. Original API regressions check the configured limit.
changeLog.reason: The engine needs the original escape and quote context to distinguish escaped dollars/backticks and braced variables from literal text without context-specific decoding state. Nested parameter quotes must not close the enclosing span or reset its depth accounting.

changeLog.change: Add parse-time expansion_line metadata to SimpleCommand and Redirect, retaining the consumed-token end line before lookahead. Anchor simple diagnostics at their first complete command element, compound redirect lists at their final target, subshell redirects at the closing parenthesis, and brace function redirects at the opening brace. Other non-subshell function-body redirects intentionally omit the line as GNU Bash does. Preserve all upstream test assertions; test-built AST constructors now supply explicit synthetic diagnostic lines. Add original API metadata regressions.
changeLog.reason: A command physical start span or redirect-local target span cannot reproduce GNU Bash expansion diagnostic lines for multiline commands and stored functions. Preserve the grammar-selected source anchor once, without rescanning source or changing parser token/escape semantics. The redirect annotation pass consumes the existing parser fuel/cancellation budget.

changeLog.change: Carry original typed literal-escape metadata from lexical emission through word tokens, quote/glob transformations, parser lookahead and assignment-value slices. A structural word cursor preserves escaped characters as protected literal parts and ends expansion names at escape boundaries without adding in-band protection markers. Backslash-newline remains a continuation. Preserve existing token spellings and upstream assertions; add original API controls for partial literal protection, variable boundaries, quoted continuations, UTF-8, syntax characters, assignment/index spellings, reserved words and operators. Metadata work uses the existing parser and shared request budgets; the unescaped path adds no work.
changeLog.reason: Deferred IFS splitting requires the lexical protection of every escaped character, not only escaped glob characters. Quote-removed token text cannot recover that protection or distinguish escaped quote bytes from source quote delimiters. The transport and cursor keep metadata bounded by token length and avoid context-specific raw-source reparsing.

changeLog.classification: Original ParameterHeader helper and regression tests in the owned Bashkit-derived lexer/API adapter; no additional upstream implementation copied.
changeLog.change: Track target-header and subscript context separately for each nested unquoted parameter. Reuse the existing ordinary single-quote handler for brackets in scalar operands rather than treating them as array subscripts. Retain raw single quotes in actual target subscripts, the original literal-escape metadata, quote/escape emission and all upstream assertions. Add controls for all trim operators, nested and malformed bracket patterns, target arrays/lengths, literal apostrophe spans and partial escape protection. Bump parser to 0.0.4.
changeLog.reason: Quoted opening/closing braces in basic scalar bracket patterns must stay inside the operand. ParameterHeader frames use the existing nesting ceiling, and each frame transition runs in the already budgeted lexer character loop; no new sentinel or reparsing path is added.

changeLog.classification: Original parser boundary correction and regression tests in the owned Bashkit-derived replacement operand scanner.
changeLog.change: Stop replacement operands at the outer closing brace while nesting only nested ${...} operands, and keep backslashes literal inside single-quoted spans. Add parser regressions for bare braces and escaped single-quote boundaries with following words. Preserve existing quote, escape, slash and upstream parser behavior.
changeLog.reason: Bash replacement operands do not treat bare braces as nested syntax, and backslashes have no escape role inside single quotes. Counting either incorrectly swallows the replacement boundary and can silently change argv or reject a command that Bash accepts.

changeLog.classification: Original quoted-parameter lexer correction and regression tests in the owned Bashkit-derived lexer.
changeLog.change: Track each nested quoted parameter header with the existing bounded ParameterHeader stack. Bare braces stay literal rather than consuming nesting depth. Apostrophes in replacement and pattern operands protect dollars and backslashes, while ordinary default operands retain literal-apostrophe expansion behavior. Add quoted bare-brace and literal ${ / $( boundary regressions; preserve existing depth ceilings and upstream assertions. The replacement operand parser likewise skips substitution scanning and nesting changes inside single quotes; an exact operand-boundary regression rejects swallowing the outer brace.
changeLog.reason: The quoted lexer must agree with replacement operand parsing: only ${ starts a nested parameter, and single-quoted replacement text must not invoke substitution scanners or swallow the outer double quote. Operator-specific quote handling preserves ordinary default-operand behavior.

changeLog.classification: Original fixed-capacity incremental nested-parameter boundary adapter and regressions; no additional upstream implementation copied.
changeLog.change: Use one fixed-capacity quote/operator state machine for both lexer parameter readers, parser default/pattern/replacement operands, and engine lazy scalar-token boundaries. Only ${ opens a nested frame. Retain each frame's double-quote, apostrophe, pattern and enclosing context. Apostrophe spans are opaque to boundary scanning; selected ordinary outer-double-quoted defaults still expand their contents lazily, while real single quotes retain literal semantics. An explicit inner double quote resets inherited pattern context for nested defaults. Slash delimiters belong only to an unquoted root replacement pattern. Preserve raw quote spelling and retain ANSI-C decoding as a protected-literal representation transform, not a separate parameter boundary reader. Parse admitted lazy scalar tokens with their enclosing quote/pattern context instead of inventing a top-level word. Add nested replacement/default, replacement/replacement, raw double-quote/apostrophe, admitted-token context and fixed-depth controls.
changeLog.reason: Replacement support introduced nested scalar tokens whose literal braces and substitution lookalikes were incorrectly interpreted by the older generic operand boundary readers. Matching boundaries before lazy evaluation must follow the same per-parameter quote context as direct replacement parsing without recursion, candidate strings, reparsing, or a reset depth allowance.

changeLog.classification: Original bounded parser corrections in the owned Bashkit-derived parser; no additional upstream code copied.
changeLog.change: Recognize ${#:offset:length} as substring of the scalar positional count, not length. Reject remaining same-line tokens after parse_command_list finishes a compound command or its redirects instead of silently accepting a second command without a separator. Retain every upstream assertion; add hash-slice and separator controls. Classify malformed special-parameter length spellings as delayed bad substitutions while retaining valid scalar hash trim and substring headers.
changeLog.reason: Arithmetic slice foundations use the existing parser to validate Bash shell-word <(...)/>(...) boundaries; silently accepting (x)+(y) or (x)>=(y) would miss Bash fatal lexical errors. State scalar/special/positional interfaces remain the semantic source.

changeLog.classification: Original explicit shell-body validation option and regression tests; no additional upstream implementation copied.
changeLog.change: Limit the arithmetic separator check to Parser::with_strict_command_separators. Captured shell-body validation opts in, and nested command parsers inherit the policy. Preserve the original public parse default and keep every strict separator assertion through the explicit entrypoint. Propagate process-substitution syntax failures only during strict validation. Add default-policy and nested command/process-substitution controls.
changeLog.reason: The engine parses a whole script before executing alias or shopt changes. Applying the new shell-body separator check globally rejected previously accepted scripts whose command boundaries can change through aliases. Localizing validation avoids introducing incomplete runtime alias support.

changeLog.classification: Original shell grammar and scanner API corrections; GNU Bash source used only to research observable phase ordering, with no implementation copied.
changeLog.change: Consume one parenthesis from a doubled closing token in array assignments, reject unseparated opening parentheses in nested lists, and honor explicit extglob options before the first token for every pattern operator. Share the existing incremental parameter and command scanners for bounded lexical substring checks before lazy selection; retain a typed ShellWord failure separately from ordinary syntax errors. Make parser fuel internally mutable so infallible word readers and their bounded child parsers consume the same fuel, request budget and cancellation checks. Expose the command scanner for admitted, cooperative expansion checks. Use the existing recovering parser to retain complete earlier lines on word syntax failures. Keep word-error recovery outside recursive grammar frames so existing hard-cap stack assertions remain intact. All upstream assertions retained.
changeLog.reason: Substring text has an outer word-reading pass and a later brace-extraction pass. Arithmetic substitutions are opaque to the former; invalid shell grammar must retain Bash fatal status 127 or 1 at the correct stage, including skipped defaults and unused functions, without test-case or prefix heuristics.

changeLog.classification: Original arithmetic field delimiter correction; no additional upstream implementation copied.
changeLog.change: Ignore parentheses, braces, colons and question marks inside quoted or escaped portions while finding a substring offset or length boundary. Retain raw quote spelling for lazy operand evaluation. Add direct AST and Bash differential regression controls.
changeLog.reason: An unused quoted operand containing an unmatched parenthesis raised the substring field depth and swallowed the enclosing brace, so arithmetic received a spurious closing brace even when the operand was skipped.

changeLog.classification: Original structural quote-protection and word-phase adapters in the owned Bashkit-derived parser; no additional upstream implementation copied. Base remains everruns/bashkit crates/bashkit/src/parser at 491c3281f668b76d64b15210b8f5d7bf97244be0.
changeLog.change: Replace quoted-glob backslash insertion with existing lexical quote boundaries decoded to literal data and part_quoted flags. Remove obsolete assignment glob-unescaping, preserving real source backslashes, and retain empty quoted prefixes beside brace groups. Retain raw spelling on every word, including the first token and words following function definitions, so brace expansion can run before parameter-name and operand-boundary parsing. Add an admitted, fuel/depth-bounded single-word lexical reparse API with an inert removable prefix; preserve quoted empty results and reject extra tokens or deferred syntax failures without parsing command grammar. Replace the deliberate top-level source-discard assertion with source-retention coverage; update two marker-helper expectations to stop requiring invented backslashes. All other existing assertions retained. Preserve lexical ANSI-C quote boundaries and recognize dollar-opened syntax across removed line continuations; keep quoted literal dollars protected. Keep ANSI-C control escape decoding separate from quote-boundary consumption; add original API controls for escaped apostrophes and continued dollar openers. All prior assertions retained. Expose single-quote parameter-scan context so continuation removal does not change single-quoted data.
changeLog.reason: Brace alternatives must distinguish quoted commas/braces from active punctuation without encoding protection in string data. Brace expansion also precedes variable-name recognition and balanced source ${...} skipping, which the later expansion AST cannot reconstruct. Raw source plus bounded word-only reparsing preserves that phase ordering without changing parameter operand semantics or adding pathname/tilde execution support. Early brace processing also needs the same lexical quote/continuation boundaries as ordinary source words; literal quote protection and source boundaries must survive decoding. Outer-double-quoted ANSI-C operand extraction remains a separate approved follow-up.

changeLog.classification: Original typed-resource adapters and regression tests in the owned Bashkit-derived parser; no additional upstream implementation copied. Parser base remains everruns/bashkit crates/bashkit/src/parser at 491c3281f668b76d64b15210b8f5d7bf97244be0.
changeLog.change: Represent parser fuel, AST/lexical parameter depth, parameter-boundary/command fuel and depth, and conditional-depth failures as typed ResourceLimit errors at their original rejection sites. Preserve public lexer error-token text with sticky typed state and retain existing diagnostic message bodies. Expanded-word reparsing bounds prefix allocation and shares its work allowance across child parsers; sticky resource failures cannot be hidden by earlier deferred syntax errors. Remove parser and engine string-prefix resource classification. Add API controls distinguishing resource failures from generated syntax errors, aggregate child work and deeply nested inactive defaults.
changeLog.reason: Brace-generated words must report resource exhaustion as explicit status 2 while retaining Bash status 1 for generated expansion syntax failures. A lower reparse nesting cap rejected already-accepted inactive operands; ordinary source parsing and generated reparsing now share the initial parser ceiling. Typed origins make this distinction structural rather than dependent on diagnostic wording.

changeLog.classification: Original arithmetic-boundary extension to the owned incremental substitution scanner and its parser/lexer call sites; no additional upstream implementation copied. Parser base remains everruns/bashkit crates/bashkit/src/parser at 491c3281f668b76d64b15210b8f5d7bf97244be0.
changeLog.change: Distinguish arithmetic substitution parentheses from command-substitution code, including nested substitutions, rather than treating arithmetic identifiers as shell keywords or shifts as heredoc operators. Incrementally replay ambiguous arithmetic as command code from a shared source tape, preserving full case/comment/heredoc state and resolved fallback openers. Expose each replay step and EOF fallback to caller work/cancellation admission, retain typed resource errors, and resolve byte-accurate lexer lookahead without consuming suffix text. Protect escaped dollars and keep lexical state per code frame. Process substitutions retain command-only initialization. Add original scanner/API controls for shifts, keyword-shaped arithmetic names, command-subshell ambiguity, protected dollars, continuations, Unicode offsets and replay fuel.
changeLog.reason: The brace generator exposed initial-lexer failures in arithmetic inside double quotes or parameter operands. Independent review then identified lost case grammar during ambiguous command-subshell fallback and escaped-dollar boundary errors; the generator now systematically produces the class at bounded nesting depths. Shared structural scanning fixes these distinctions without dropping controls or adding exemptions. Explicit replay work prevents hidden uncancellable rescans and speculative candidate-copy growth.

changeLog.classification: Original changes to the owned substitution scanner, lexer and parser; semantics from GNU Bash 5.3 parse.y (parse_comsub, parse_matched_pair with P_ARITH) and subst.c (chk_arithsub), observed against /usr/bin/bash 5.3.15; no upstream code copied. Parser base remains everruns/bashkit crates/bashkit/src/parser at 491c3281f668b76d64b15210b8f5d7bf97244be0.
changeLog.change: Replace the arithmetic-to-command replay with bash's model: a fused $(( or <(( span ends by raw parenthesis matching (quotes and nested $( respected; ${ is plain text inside it), and only then is classified as arithmetic (final inner close plus chk_arithsub balance) or as command text. Command-classified fused bodies that fail to parse become WordPart::UnparsedCommandSubstitution instead of rejecting the script. Every other $( and <( body, including bodies inside ${...} operands and nested in raw $(( text, is parsed with the script; its syntax error is Error::ShellWord (status 127). An unterminated span is 127 when bash's parse of the bodies it already read, or of the outermost open command frame, stops at a token, and the EOF error (2) otherwise. Parser::with_strict_substitution_bodies parses substitution bodies with strict separators while a whole-script top level stays lenient. Nested substitution parses run after each word's scan loop returns, and grammar functions on the recursive path keep temporaries in out-of-line helpers (debug per-level stack about 21 KB to 7 KB). Lexer substitution scanning is charged one work unit per character.
changeLog.reason: The brace generator's boundary matrix (closing-count variants) showed bash rejects or accepts these spans by raw paren matching and reports comsub syntax errors with status 127; the replay accepted comment-hidden parentheses. A stricter hard-depth test overflowed the 2 MiB debug test stack before the AST cap.

changeLog.classification: Original changes to the owned parser for command and process substitution; semantics from GNU Bash 5.3 parse.y (parse_comsub, parse_matched_pair with P_DOLBRACE/LEX_GTLT, print_comsub) and subst.c (extract_process_subst via xparse_dolparen), observed against /usr/bin/bash 5.3.15; no upstream code copied. Parser base remains everruns/bashkit crates/bashkit/src/parser at 491c3281f668b76d64b15210b8f5d7bf97244be0.
changeLog.change: Add Parser::parse_substitution_token_with_limits and parse_backtick_body_with_limits so the engine parses $(...) tokens and backtick bodies found in lazy operand text with the word reader's own classification. Scan <( and >( bodies in every ${...} operand at parse time (not only substring operands) and store them printed back as bash does (comsub_commands, which keeps a case statement's first clause on its case line). The substitution boundary scanner opens a frame for <( and >( after a single angle bracket, so a fused <(( span is raw paren-matched like $((. A fused <((/>(( body that is not a command list becomes WordPart::UnparsedProcessSubstitution instead of an empty substitution. Unterminated operand spans report bash's EOF error (2) unless the open command text stops at a token (127). Here-documents read inside substitution bodies end at a line that is the delimiter followed by ')'. A line continuation in a here-document delimiter joins it instead of quoting a newline. Subshells and brace groups stop at a token no command can start with instead of looping until fuel runs out, and an empty subshell is a syntax error. Backtick bodies whose converted $(...) text would not close at its own ')' (here-documents, quotes) are deferred like unparsable bodies. select accepts newlines before in, no in list ("$@") and a { } body, like for.
changeLog.reason: The substitution-boundary generator (scripts/fuzz-shell-substitution-boundaries.mjs) compared against Bash 5.3.15 once command substitution executed: these were the parse-time differences in its mismatch classes, including parser fuel exhaustion on '( ; )'.

changeLog.classification: Original parser safety correction in the owned Bashkit-derived parser; no upstream implementation copied.
changeLog.change: Reject a case-body token that cannot start a command instead of retrying the same token until parser fuel exhaustion.

GNU Bash builtins/pushd.def: pushd_builtin, popd_builtin, dirs_builtin, get_dirstack_index (same)
shellDirectories.strategy: Logical-mode cd over the existing host stat contract: lexical canonicalization that requires a directory before each .. and at the result, host-reported search permission, and the raw path's real error when canonicalization fails. The cwd field is updated directly first; OLDPWD and PWD then publish through the existing admitted assignment path, and a readonly binding fails the command without undoing the change. Each stack version is one immutable Rc value owning its entries and one StorageAllocation ticket on the State memory budget for the Rc box, vector slots and string capacities. A change admits the next version's requested bytes before allocating it, reconciles recorded excess vector capacity into the ticket, and publishes only on success. Clone and State::snapshot share the version; changes build an admitted copy. pushd dir and popd prepare the next version before cd and publish it only after cd succeeds; no-argument and rotating pushd change the stack before cd, as Bash does. Work admission covers only transient copies, and the async paths take cooperative checkpoints; option parsing is synchronous.
shellDirectories.deferred: cd -P/-e and the physical raw-path retry need symlink resolution, which the filesystem contract lacks; they fail explicitly. CDPATH tilde entries, the DIRSTACK array (variables family), pwd -L/-P, and decoupled PWD values remain unsupported. See docs/directories.md.

shellDeclarationAppend.classification: Original Rust scalar declaration append adapter and scope-aware state view. GNU Bash is a behavior oracle; no upstream implementation copied or adapted.
shellDeclarationAppend.strategy: Recognize scalar += declaration words without splitting their RHS. Resolve current local namerefs before selecting the target scope. Read only the current local or inherited function-prefix value for a local append; ordinary declarations read the visible scalar target. Admit and cooperatively scan before state-owned assignment for repeated locals, preserving indexed element zero and raw references. Record prefix-owner provenance separately from ordinary locals. Compound array declarations and explicit -n appends remain separate work.

shellTilde.classification: Original HOME-only tilde adapter and controls. GNU Bash 5.3.15 is a behavior oracle; no upstream implementation copied or adapted.
shellTilde.implementation: Recognize unquoted HOME tilde prefixes from existing literal parts after brace expansion. Words changed by brace expansion keep only a leading prefix, because Bash gives them fresh flags without assignment eligibility. Snapshot the actual scalar binding at each eligible literal execution segment, following preceding parameter side effects. Protect only substituted home bytes from splitting and pathname expansion. Scalar assignments allow prefixes after literal colons; ordinary words allow this only after an unquoted valid identifier and equals or plus-equals. Declarations and redirect scalar words retain ordinary assignment-looking recognition; only actual scalar RHSs use assignment mode. Admit the retained snapshot before copying and charge each emitted copy to existing raw, field, work and storage budgets. Words without an unquoted literal tilde spend no tilde work; assignment-name scans, tilde candidates and emitted values yield and check cancellation. Normal PR41 integration routes actual scalar-form RHS values, including scalar += and scalar writes through indexed bindings, through the same assignment expansion context without changing subscript evaluation, append, binding storage or compound/list expansion.
shellTilde.deferred: Named-user homes and HOME-unset account fallback require an authentic runtime account lookup; preserve those prefixes literally. PWD/OLDPWD, directory-stack forms, parameter operands, compound/list array assignments and non-UTF-8 fields remain outside this slice. Only the separately recorded empty-quote retention changes parser behavior. No AST, state storage, FileSubstitution or pathname traversal changes.
shellTilde.gate: Record actual local Bash 5.3.15(1)-release controls once and replay CI without live Bash. The tilde and extglob recorders share the original scripts/recorded-bash.ts runner. Native/WASI resource and cancellation controls plus actual Waffle controls and the unchanged full serial 9221-row frozen scored-only replay. Preserve all former passes, identities, ordered membership, skips and historical diagnostic payloads.

shellPathname.classification: Original argv pathname admission, sparse quote masks, noglob option and Waffle controls. GNU Bash 5.3.15 is a behavior oracle, not copied implementation. Directory streaming and the basic-only pathname compiler reuse the existing original glob.rs and the local adaptation recorded in shellParameterTrim.
shellPathname.implementation: Unquoted non-scalar fields that can run substitutions expand pathnames for command names, arguments, indexed compound assignment operands, for-lists and file-substitution targets unless set -f or set -o noglob is active. Fields track quote protection as (bytes, protected) runs, charged only for admitted words like their other buffers, and expand them into an admitted byte mask only when an unprotected *, ? or [ occurs, so plain argv keeps its exact budgets and is returned unchanged. Admitted words with extglob on also send @(, +( and !( groups to the existing explicit rejection. The glob step knows whether its fields were storage-admitted: unadmitted argv slots are not charged, discarded text is not released and matched names are released, while admitted for-list and file-substitution accounting is unchanged. Matches are sorted bytewise, dot files need an explicit leading dot and nullglob removes only unquoted unmatched patterns. A component needing more characters than any path matches nothing and is read without building its pattern; candidate paths longer than any path, not counting a directory's trailing slash, are absent, while budget and storage failures stay errors. Scalar assignment and redirect words stay scalar.
shellPathname.deferred: Pathname extglob, dotglob, globstar, nocaseglob, failglob, GLOBIGNORE and set -o listing remain unsupported. With extglob on, argv fields containing extglob groups stay literal as before, while admitted for-list and file-substitution words keep the explicit unsupported status 2.
shellPathname.gate: Forty-one independent Bash-versus-production-Waffle controls, a native runtime control and the unchanged frozen 9221-case per-ID production replay. Only proven gained baseline outcomes and derived counts change; historical diagnostic payloads remain intact.

shellLastArgument.classification: Original command-completion adapter. GNU Bash 5.3.15 is a behavior oracle; no upstream implementation copied or adapted. Thirty fixture scripts are adapted from the frozen Brush corpus.
shellLastArgument.strategy: Retain the admitted expanded last argument, then publish it through ordinary binding storage after dispatch. Builtin prefix frames remain active until publication reaches their temporary nameref targets, then restore the caller bindings. Automatic publication uses the existing numeric OPTIND publication policy without applying explicit-assignment cursor resets. External dispatch clones its retained command name once for argv and borrows the original for diagnostics. Assignment-only commands publish an empty value. Preserve internal dispatch errors, terminal cancellation and resource outcomes, pipeline/subshell isolation, readonly target diagnostics and export clearing. Startup uses the actual shell name unless the environment supplied _. No runtime facts or command add-ons are introduced.

shellCaseAttributes.strategy: Keep lower/upper metadata in state, save and restore it with locals, admit it in snapshots, and map owned scalar values before assignment publication. Reuse the existing bounded locale mapper moved unchanged below expansion. Preserve attribute-only values and expose case metadata through named declaration and parameter-transform rendering.

shellIndexedSlices.classification: Original local sparse indexed slice adapter and recorded GNU Bash 5.3.15 observations. No external implementation copied or adapted.
shellIndexedSlices.implementation: Sparse numeric offsets seek through the existing borrowed state reader. Length counts present entries, not holes. Empty sources and out-of-range offsets skip bound arithmetic. Selected strings are admitted before copying and emitted through shared quote/list/IFS logic with cooperative cancellation and command-wide limits. Scalar bindings keep existing text slicing. PIPESTATUS reads its existing producer. No indexed state mutation or durable producer publication API changes.

shellPromptTransformation.classification: Original prompt decoder and scanner context; GNU Bash 5.3.15 is a behavior oracle. No upstream implementation copied or adapted.
shellPromptTransformation.implementation: Decode scalar @P escapes into admitted UTF-8 bytes, then expand through the existing bounded substitution scanner with literal prompt quotes. State owns promptvars and inherits it into subshells. Cwd, HOME and PROMPT_DIRTRIM determine directory escapes; available USER, HOSTNAME and EUID bindings supply identity escapes without synthesized facts. Protect fact text before substitution scanning. Existing outer field rules apply to the final result. Nested scalar transformations use the operand scanner.

shellPromptTransformation.gate: Pinned Bash 5.3.15 recordings through production Waffle, native recursion/output/cancellation/missing-fact controls, and the unchanged hosted frozen 9221-case replay.
